regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"India GDP at 7.8% YoY looks like acceleration — until you note the RBI's own forecast sits 110bps lower at 6.7% YoY, and IIP YoY decelerated to 6.7% from 8.8% the prior month. PMI composite at 54.6 is services-led (54.5) while manufacturing slips to 52.8; core sector at 5.4% YoY, down from 6.0%, confirms goods-economy momentum is fading. The quality of this growth is narrowing: if services PMI softens one more print, the headline GDP story loses its last credible pillar.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY — a 95th-percentile print, up from 20.05% — is the number that makes the RBI's 5.25% repo rate look increasingly inadequate. Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY sits above the 4% midpoint target, but the real danger is the wedge: WPI at 9.92% YoY means producer-price pressure is building a pipeline that CPI hasn't fully absorbed. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY appears contained — but with Brent at $102.7/bbl and iron ore jumping from $96.59 to $161.91/t, that containment is borrowed time.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% YoY — a 630bps divergence — has pushed the CD ratio to 81.4%, the 75th percentile of its 10-year range. The last time this ratio sustained above 80% during a rate-hold cycle, the system eventually faced forced deposit-rate hikes that compressed NIMs and triggered bank earnings downgrades. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% signals the pressure is migrating: wholesale funding costs will rise before the RBI formally tightens, and smaller NBFCs with no bond-market access will feel it first.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. has been on hold, but the real rate is being eroded by fuel and WPI inflation faster than the MPC's communiqués acknowledge — the RBI's own inflation forecast just revised up to 5.1% YoY from 4.6%. A negative real rate environment with a CD ratio at the 75th percentile and INR at 96.15 is not a stable equilibrium: either deposit rates rise organically (compressing bank margins) or the RBI is forced to signal tightening to defend the currency. The market is pricing neither outcome.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation rising to 77.4% of capacity — the 74th percentile, historically the threshold at which private capex announcements accelerate — is the most unambiguously positive signal in today's data. Credit to industry at 20.0% YoY and credit to services at 22.9% YoY confirm this is being financed, not just announced. The inversion worth watching: core sector growth slowing to 5.4% YoY from 6.0% means the upstream inputs (steel, cement, power) are not yet confirming the capex surge — either the lag is normal or the IIP capital goods number is front-running reality.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month and passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY, two-wheelers at 19.7% YoY signal broad demand — but GST must be decomposed before celebration. At ₹1,99,853 cr, collections are at the 71st percentile, not a record, and the prior month's ₹1,74,116 cr base was weak, flattering the YoY. Two-wheeler growth at 19.7% YoY is the more honest consumption signal: it reaches the mass-market rural and semi-urban buyer that GST formalization effects don't fully capture. The divergence between strong vehicle sales and credit-card growth slowing to 2.3% YoY suggests urban discretionary spending is rotating from revolving credit to asset purchases — a quality shift, not a demand surge.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 630 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (down from 82.5% prior month) remains elevated at 75th percentile of 10-year range. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months. NBFC credit growth accelerating at 14.9% YoY (up from 10.6% YoY) signals wholesale funding pressure migrating to non-bank lenders.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they will poach deposits from smaller peers. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; liquidity stress will force asset sales or margin compression. RBI will likely ease liquidity via OMOs or CRR cuts within 6-8 weeks if deposit growth doesn't accelerate. Position for a 25-50 bps rate cut by Q3 FY27.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically precedes either deposit acceleration or credit slowdown. Last time it was this elevated (2022), RBI eased within 10 weeks.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY (latest) with capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6% prior month) signals robust investment demand. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6% prior month) is moderating but remains positive. Credit to industry at 20% YoY (up from 6.5% YoY) and credit to services at 22.9% YoY (up from 10.2% YoY) confirm broad-based capex financing. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is at 74th percentile — historically the sweet spot for new capex announcements.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks. Increase exposure to project-linked equities (L&T, Larsen, Godrej & Boyce). Expect order book visibility to extend 18-24 months. Avoid defensive plays; cyclical upside outweighs near-term margin pressure from input costs. Capex cycle typically runs 18-24 months from this utilisation level.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is near the 10-year median and historically precedes 12-18 months of sustained capex growth. Last similar cycle (2016-17) saw capex growth sustain for 20 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit Record; Affluent Money Entering","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (up from ₹31,961 cr / month prior month), rising 2 consecutive months. SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (up from ₹18.21 lakh cr), also rising 2 consecutive months at 93rd percentile. SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (up from 99.06 mn) at 82nd percentile. However, SIP YoY growth at 14% (down from 16% prior month) signals deceleration. MF AUM at ₹87.08 lakh cr (rising 2 consecutive months) at 86th percentile. DII equity net flows at ₹58,502 cr net / month (up from ₹35,099 cr net / month) at 100th percentile — highest on record.","implication":"SIP accounts growing 25% but SIP AUM growing 40% — average ticket size rising sharply, indicating affluent retail entering, not mass-market expansion. This is late-cycle behaviour. Overweight large-cap, quality dividend stocks; underweight small-cap momentum plays. Expect SIP growth to decelerate further as base effects kick in. DII flows at record highs suggest domestic institutional confidence — use this window to trim overvalued mid-caps.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP AUM at 93rd percentile and DII flows at all-time high. Historically, when DII flows exceed ₹50,000 cr / month, equity valuations compress 8-12% within 3-6 months as retail profit-taking follows.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI Comfort","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% YoY prior month) at 95th percentile — highest in 10-year range. WPI at 9.92% YoY (up from 9.78% YoY) at 67th percentile. Brent crude at $102.7/bbl (flat from prior month) but trending within $96–$103/bbl range over past 6 months. Natural gas at $2.936/MMBtu (flat) at 18th percentile — historically low. Iron ore at $161.91/t (up from $96.59/t) signals China demand recovery. Copper at $6.571/lb (flat) at 78th percentile.","implication":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile will keep RBI's inflation forecast elevated (currently 5.1% YoY, up from 4.6% YoY). This constrains rate-cut timing to Q3 FY27 at earliest. Hedge energy exposure via long crude positions or energy stocks (ONGC, Reliance). Avoid consumer discretionary stocks with high fuel-cost pass-through risk. Monitor Brent above $105/bbl as a trigger for RBI to hold rates longer.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile historically preceded 6-8 weeks of RBI hawkishness. Last time (2022), RBI held rates for 5 consecutive meetings despite growth concerns.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"Fed Tightening Bias Resurfaces; Carry Unwind Risk","data_text":"US 10-year Treasury yield at 5.29% yield (up from 5.26% prior month) at 96th percentile — highest in 10-year range. Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (up from 3.63% p.a.) at 68th percentile. Fed balance sheet at $6,743.031 bn (flat, rising 4 in a row) at 47th percentile. US CPI at 3.353% YoY (up from 3.3039% YoY) at 53rd percentile; US core CPI at 2.4462% YoY (down from 2.4665% YoY) at 47th percentile. BOJ rate at 1% p.a. (up from 0.75% p.a.) at 86th percentile — strong-negative signal. ECB deposit rate at 2.25% p.a. (up from 2% p.a.) at 59th percentile.","implication":"US 10-year yield at 96th percentile signals carry-trade unwind risk. INR/USD at 96.15 (up from 95.93) is already under pressure. Reduce leverage in emerging-market carry trades. Overweight USD-denominated assets; underweight INR-denominated bonds. BOJ tightening (1% p.a.) will reduce JPY carry supply — expect INR volatility to spike 200-300 bps. Hedge FX exposure via 3-month forwards; avoid long-duration rupee debt.","pct_10y":96,"pct_note":"US 10-year yield at 96th percentile and BOJ tightening at 86th percentile historically precede 4-8 week periods of EM currency weakness. Last similar episode (2023) saw INR depreciate 3.2% in 6 weeks.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakening; RBI Intervention Likely Soon","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 ₹ (up from 95.93 ₹ prior month) at 91st percentile — near 10-year highs. INR has weakened 3 of last 5 periods. DXY at 102.06 index (flat, rising 4 of last 5 periods) at 55th percentile. FII equity net flows at ₹29,631 cr net / month (up from ₹20,200 cr net / month) at 83rd percentile, but this masks recent volatility (recent: -114 → -3,111.9 → +29,631). India VIX at 14.455 index (up from 13.49) at 10th percentile — historically low, suggesting complacency.","implication":"INR at 96.15 is approaching RBI's implicit 96.5 intervention threshold. Expect RBI to deploy reserves or conduct dollar sales within 2-3 weeks if INR breaches 96.5. FII flows are volatile; the recent ₹29,631 cr inflow may reverse if US yields stay elevated. Reduce INR short positions; hedge via 3-month forwards at 96.5-97 levels. India VIX at 10th percentile suggests low hedging cost — buy 1-month INR puts at 97 strike.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 91st percentile historically precedes RBI intervention within 2-4 weeks. Last time INR hit 96+ (2023), RBI sold $5 bn in reserves over 3 weeks to stabilise the currency.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Shift, Not IT Weakness","data_text":"Office absorption at 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter (down from 13.7 mn sq ft / quarter) at 6th percentile — historically weak. Office vacancy at 14.5% vacant (down from 15.1% vacant) at 42nd percentile. However, retail mall vacancy at 4.8% vacant (down from 5% vacant) at 7th percentile — near 10-year lows. Rent in Bengaluru at ₹163/sqft/mo (up from ₹148/sqft/mo) at 95th percentile; rent in Mumbai at ₹335/sqft/mo (up from ₹322/sqft/mo) at 100th percentile — both at all-time highs. Nifty IT index is flat YTD despite office absorption collapse. Bank Nifty at 54,450.75 index (down from 54,633) at 89th percentile — strong-positive signal despite equity weakness.","implication":"Office absorption is collapsing NOT because IT services are dying, but because Global Capability Centres (GCCs) are consolidating into fewer, larger campuses in Bengaluru and Mumbai. Traditional IT services firms are shrinking footprints; GCCs (Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Apple) are expanding. This explains why rents in Tier-1 cities are at all-time highs while overall absorption is weak. Retail mall vacancy at 7th percentile signals consumer spending is robust — consistent with GST at ₹199,853 cr / month. Implication: Avoid traditional IT office REITs (Embassy, Mindspace); overweight retail REITs and consumer discretionary. Bank Nifty strength at 89th percentile suggests credit cycle is intact despite office weakness — credit is flowing to GCCs and retail, not legacy IT.","pct_10y":6,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 6th percentile would normally signal recession; however, retail vacancy at 7th percentile and rents at all-time highs indicate sectoral rotation, not demand collapse. This divergence has not occurred in the past 10 years — it is a structural shift in India's real estate demand.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Services Carry the Growth Story — Goods Economy Quietly Fades

The facts:

  • PMI Composite at 54.6 is services-driven (PMI Services 54.5); PMI Manufacturing slipped to 52.8 from 53.5, a two-month low.
  • IIP YoY decelerated to 6.7% YoY from 8.8%; core sector at 5.4% YoY, down from 6.0% — goods-economy momentum is narrowing.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY and PV sales at 16% YoY confirm mass-market demand holds; credit-card growth at 2.3% YoY (down from 5.6%) signals urban revolving credit is contracting.
  • But RBI GDP forecast at 6.7% YoY sits 110bps below the headline print of 7.8% YoY — the regulator's own model does not believe the number.

The tension: Headline GDP at 7.8% YoY is services-and-statistics; the goods economy — IIP, core sector, manufacturing PMI — is decelerating in unison. The two cannot diverge indefinitely without a downward revision to the headline.

Bottom line: Watch PMI Services: a print below 53 would collapse the last pillar supporting the 7.8% YoY narrative and force consensus GDP downgrades.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

Bond Markets Win the Argument — DM Equities Finally Capitulate

The facts:

  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.29% yield — 96th percentile of its 10-year range, up from 5.26% — is tightening financial conditions faster than any rate decision.
  • Euro Stoxx 50 fell to 6,175 from a 100th-percentile 6,269; S&P 500 flat at 7,666 at its own 100th percentile — the divergence between US and European equity resilience is narrowing.
  • US GDP SAAR at 2.2% SAAR (rising from 1.5%) contradicts the bond market's distress signal; US core CPI at 2.4% YoY is falling — the Fed's inflation problem is easing even as yields climb.
  • But BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile, up from 0.75%) is unwinding the yen carry trade that funded EM positioning — India's INR at 96.15 is in the crossfire within 60–90 days.

The tension: US growth is re-accelerating on GDP SAAR while core inflation falls — a soft-landing signal. Yet 10Y yields at 5.29% and BOJ tightening are tightening global financial conditions independently of the Fed. The equity market is pricing the soft landing; the bond and FX markets are pricing the tightening.

Bottom line: If US 10Y breaches 5.35% yield, expect EM carry unwind to accelerate — watch INR and FII equity flows as the leading indicators.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Liquidity at Record Highs — But the Fuel Tank Is Thinning

The facts:

  • DII equity net flows at ₹58,502 cr net / month — a 100th-percentile, all-time record — absorbed the market's weakness; SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile), rising two consecutive months.
  • SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (93rd percentile); MF AUM at ₹87.08 lakh cr (86th percentile) — the domestic institutional bid is structurally deep.
  • But SIP YoY growth decelerated to 14% YoY from 16% — the marginal rate of new money entering is slowing even as the stock grows.
  • FII equity net at ₹29,631 cr net / month (83rd percentile) masks violent intra-period swings: -₹114 cr → -₹3,112 cr → +₹29,631 cr. The FII bid is a single session, not a trend.

The tension: Record DII flows are providing a floor, but they are funded by SIP growth that is decelerating at the margin. FII flows look positive in aggregate but are concentrated and reversible. The liquidity cushion is real but thinner than the headline suggests.

Bottom line: Monitor SIP YoY growth: a third consecutive monthly deceleration below 12% YoY would signal retail participation is plateauing and the DII floor becomes less reliable.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

NRI Demand Holds Premium Residential; REITs Price Office Risk

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up 5pp vs prior period), with 25% share within premium/luxury; remittances at $73 bn (12.8% YoY) provide the funding base.
  • Premium (₹80 lakh–₹1.5 cr) and luxury (₹1.5–₹2.5 cr) together command 58% of new launch supply; Hyderabad leads sales momentum at 15% YoY with launches surging 120% YoY — a supply-demand mismatch building at 29 months of unsold inventory.
  • Bank Nifty at 54,451 (89th percentile) is holding despite Nifty 50 at 22,422 (72nd percentile) declining — banks are being priced for capex-cycle credit growth, not deposit stress.
  • But office REITs are pricing the absorption collapse: Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit (down from ₹429), Mindspace at ₹345/unit (down from ₹501), Brookfield at ₹263/unit (down from ₹330) — all three down 13–31% from prior levels.

The tension: NRI-driven premium residential demand and record retail SIPs are supporting asset prices from below; but office REIT NAVs are being marked down as GCC-led absorption (42% of occupier mix) fails to offset IT services weakness (21%). The same economy is producing divergent asset outcomes.

Bottom line: Avoid office REITs until absorption recovers above 15 mn sq ft / quarter; overweight premium residential developers with Hyderabad and Bengaluru exposure where NRI demand is concentrated.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — US Yields Hold the Match

The facts:

  • US 10Y at 5.29% yield (96th percentile) — if it breaches 5.40%, EM carry unwinds accelerate, INR tests 97–98, and FII equity flows reverse from +₹29,631 cr net / month to negative within weeks.
  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent at $102.7/bbl — a $5 move to $108 widens India's CAD by ~40bps, adds 50–70bps to CPI within two quarters, and forces the RBI's hand on rates.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile) with NBFC credit at 14.9% YoY accelerating — if deposit growth does not recover to 13%+ YoY within two quarters, expect RBI macro-prudential action on risk weights.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile) — each 25bps hike unwinds an estimated $50–100bn of yen carry globally; India's $680bn FX reserve buffer is large but not infinite against a coordinated unwind.

The tension: All three domestic risks — inflation, credit stress, currency — have a single external trigger: US 10Y yields. A yield spike compresses the RBI's room to hold rates, widens the CAD via INR depreciation, and tightens NBFC funding simultaneously.

Bottom line: Watch US 10Y Treasury this week: a close above 5.35% yield is the threshold that activates all three domestic risk channels in sequence.

"}
